l4_steps.name: Pull crew schedule and rest window data
l4_steps.input: Published crew roster and pairing assignments
l4_steps.output: Rest window dataset per crew member for next 72 hours
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew records extracted ≤15 min before duty window opens
l4_steps.pain_point: Roster amendments late in the day can invalidate pre-computed rest windows; Jeppesen batch refresh cycles may lag real-time pairing changes by up to 30 minutes

l4_steps.name: Validate minimum rest vs FAR 117.25 requirement
l4_steps.output: Rest compliance flag (Pass/Fail) per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members assigned with <10-hr rest or <8-hr sleep opportunity; compliance check completed ≥4 hrs before scheduled report time
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 117.25 requires rest free from all restraint including deadhead travel; mis-classification of deadhead as rest is a common audit finding and can trigger FAA enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Escalate non-compliant rest to Crew Scheduling
l4_steps.output: Replacement or re-routing request logged in crew scheduling queue
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of rest violations resolved ≥2 hrs before report time; zero crew members reporting for duty with open violation
l4_steps.pain_point: Replacement pool exhaustion during irregular operations forces cascading re-assignments; lack of real-time hotel check-in data makes actual sleep opportunity difficult to verify

l4_steps.name: Calculate maximum FDP from Table B/C values
l4_steps.input: Report time (local), number of scheduled flight segments, acclimation status
l4_steps.output: Maximum FDP in hours per FAR 117.13 Table B (unaugmented) or Table C (augmented)
l4_steps.kpi: FDP calculation completed ≤5 min per crew pairing; 100% of FDPs within published table limits before sign-out
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 117 Table B/C values vary by report time window; scheduling systems may default to most permissive bracket if report time is ambiguous, creating compliance risk on early-morning or red-eye pairings

l4_steps.name: Determine if augmented crew operations apply
l4_steps.input: Crew complement (2 vs 3+ pilots), planned in-flight rest facility class
l4_steps.output: Augmented operations flag and applicable FDP extension allowance
l4_steps.kpi: Augmented classification accuracy ≥99.9%; mis-classification rate <1 per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Rest facility class (Class 1/2/3) on the aircraft must match the assumption in the FDP extension; discrepancies between charter configuration and published aircraft spec cause mid-trip compliance gaps

l4_steps.name: Apply FDP extension if operationally justified
l4_steps.input: Operational need justification, augmented crew flag, crew consent
l4_steps.output: Approved FDP extension record (max 1-hr, once per calendar day per FAR 117.19)
l4_steps.kpi: FDP extensions ≤5% of total monthly pairings; no extension applied without documented crew consent
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 117.19 limits extension to once per calendar day and requires crew concurrence; pressure from operations control to extend without concurrence is a recurring safety culture risk

l4_steps.name: Authorize FDP and issue pre-departure brief
l4_steps.input: Validated FDP, rest compliance records, pairing details
l4_steps.output: Signed FDP authorization record; crew brief packet distributed
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew departures with FDP authorization on file; brief packet delivered ≥60 min before report time
l4_steps.pain_point: Digital brief distribution depends on crew mobile app connectivity; offline crews at remote outstations may not receive updates, requiring phone confirmation fallback

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time duty time against FDP limits
l4_steps.input: Live ACARS/ADS-B block times, ATC delay feeds, gate departure confirmations
l4_steps.output: Running FDP counter per crew member updated every 15 minutes
l4_steps.kpi: Real-time duty counter latency ≤15 min; alert triggered ≥30 min before projected FDP breach
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC ground delays extend FDP without triggering automatic alerts if block-out time is used as the FDP clock start; ambiguity between pushback and engine-start as FDP trigger creates audit exposure

l4_steps.name: Receive and log crew fatigue self-declaration
l4_steps.input: Crew member fatigue declaration via crew portal or ACARS datalink
l4_steps.output: Fatigue event record with timestamp, flight number, and crew ID
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of fatigue declarations acknowledged by Crew Tracking within 10 min; zero declarations closed without resolution note
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 117.9 gives crew unlimited authority to declare fatigue; ground pressure to continue operations despite declaration is a safety culture issue tracked in ASAP/SMS; anonymous reporting gap remains if crew fear punitive response

l4_steps.name: Coordinate AOC for substitution or flight delay
l4_steps.input: Fatigue declaration or projected FDP breach from steps 3.1–3.2
l4_steps.output: Replacement crew assignment or delay/cancellation decision logged in AOC system
l4_steps.kpi: Replacement crew sourced ≤90 min from declaration for flights with >2 hrs to departure; cancellation rate due to fatigue <0.1% of monthly operations
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve pools at outstations are thin; during IROPS a single fatigue declaration can cascade into multi-flight cancellations if no qualified crew is within legal deadhead range

l4_steps.name: Calculate 60-hr limit in 168 consecutive hours
l4_steps.input: Historical flight duty records for prior 168 hours per crew member
l4_steps.output: Rolling 60-hr utilisation figure per crew member; alert if ≥85% (51 hrs)
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members exceeding 60-hr limit; alert threshold triggered at 51 hrs to allow scheduling intervention
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen rolling-window calculation relies on accurate block-in times; late ACARS updates during IROPS create data gaps that cause the 168-hr window to be computed from estimated rather than actual times

l4_steps.name: Calculate 190-hr limit in 672 consecutive hours
l4_steps.input: Historical flight duty records for prior 672 hours per crew member
l4_steps.output: Rolling 190-hr utilisation figure; alert if ≥85% (162 hrs)
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members exceeding 190-hr limit in any 28-day window; alert generated ≥10 days before projected breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew pick-up flying during high-demand periods (holiday banks, peak summer) can push cumulative limits faster than monthly bidding models project; late additions to open-time are the primary cause of 190-hr violations

l4_steps.name: Track annual 1,000-hr flight time limit
l4_steps.input: Year-to-date flight time log per crew member (block hours)
l4_steps.output: Annual flight time projection and alert if ≥900 hrs (90% of limit)
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members exceeding 1,000 flight hours in any calendar year; 90% threshold alert issued ≥45 days before year-end for projected breaches
l4_steps.pain_point: Annual limit interacts with contract maximums and PBS bid awards; crew members approaching the limit late in Q4 reduce reserve coverage exactly when holiday operations demand peaks

l4_steps.name: Remove near-limit crew and notify Crew Planning
l4_steps.output: Crew member status updated to limit-protected; open pairings returned to scheduling pool
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of limit-alert crew removed from active schedule within 2 hrs of alert; zero limit violations in FAA audit sample
l4_steps.pain_point: Removing crew mid-rotation at an outstation forces last-minute positioning of replacements; hotel and transportation costs associated with early release are not always captured in scheduling cost models

l4_steps.name: Aggregate fatigue events in FRMS database
l4_steps.input: Fatigue declarations, FDP breaches, near-limit alerts from phases 3–4
l4_steps.output: Consolidated FRMS event dataset with route, crew base, pairing-type dimensions
l4_steps.kpi: FRMS dataset refreshed within 24 hrs of event; 100% of fatigue events linked to pairing and route data
l4_steps.pain_point: FRMS data lives in a separate analytics store from Jeppesen operational data; ETL latency and schema mismatches between crew scheduling and safety systems delay monthly trend analysis by 3–5 days

l4_steps.name: Analyse fatigue patterns by route, base, pairing type
l4_steps.output: Monthly FRMS trend report with heat-map by route and crew base
l4_steps.kpi: FRMS report issued within 5 business days of month-end; ≥3 pairing types or routes reviewed per cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Small event counts per route make statistical significance difficult to establish; safety analysts lack crew scheduling write-back access to act directly on findings without a manual change-request workflow

l4_steps.name: Revise pairings and notify Safety Review Board
l4_steps.input: FRMS trend report identifying systemic fatigue risk in specific pairings
l4_steps.output: Revised pairing set submitted for next bid period; Safety Review Board notification issued
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of systemic-risk pairings revised within 2 bid periods of identification; recurrence rate of flagged pairing type <20% after revision
l4_steps.pain_point: Pairing revisions that improve fatigue compliance may reduce utilisation efficiency and increase crew costs; trade-off approval requires VP-level sign-off which extends lead time by 2–4 weeks

l4_steps.name: Generate FAR 117 compliance report for FAA
l4_steps.input: Duty records, rest logs, FDP authorizations, fatigue event records for reporting period
l4_steps.output: FAR Part 117 compliance report (quarterly); violation summary if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Report submitted ≥5 business days before FAA due date; zero data gaps in duty record coverage
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA may request ad hoc audits beyond scheduled reporting; retrieving complete duty records for specific crew members across legacy and current systems takes 3–5 days if data spans a system migration boundary

l4_steps.name: File voluntary disclosure or corrective action plan
l4_steps.input: Identified FAR 117 violations from compliance report
l4_steps.output: FAA voluntary disclosure (ASAP) submission or corrective action plan on file
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of identified violations disclosed within 10 business days; corrective action plan implemented within 60 days of disclosure
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA ASAP program requires an established MOU with the local FSDO; airlines without an active ASAP agreement lose the enforcement mitigation benefit and face higher civil penalty exposure for self-disclosed violations
